documents.title: The Christmas-Jubilee Timing: Western Christmas + Orthodox Christmas + Cambodia's Victory over Genocide Day as Convergent Annual Anchor
documents.text:
> *Draft notes for the editor:* this is the founder-voice (thonly.org) canonical draft. Per the genre-split institutional-output convention, heartbank.net does not carry a per-paper mirror. The slug `christmas-jubilee-timing` is the canonical research URL.

---

## Abstract

This essay analyzes the convergence of four annually-recurring liberation-and-redistribution events on a single twelve-day window — **December 25 through January 7** — and argues that the convergence makes the window the maximally-resonant annual anchor for civilizational-scale redistribution rituals. The four events: (i) **Western Christmas** (December 25): the canonical Christian annual ritual of generosity, gift-giving, and family reconciliation; (ii) **Orthodox Christmas** (January 7): the Julian-calendar celebration carrying the same theological substance with twelve days of liturgical-and-civic resonance between the two dates; (iii) **Cambodia's Victory over Genocide Day** (January 7): the Cambodian national holiday commemorating liberation from the Khmer Rouge in 1979, the most consequential civic liberation event in Cambodian modern history; (iv) **the Aquarian Pool's annual emptying** (December 25 → January 7): the HeartBank institutional redistribution ritual culminating on January 7. The essay argues that the convergence is not accidental in the metaphysical sense (the calendar dates have independent historical causation) but is *structurally apt*: the institutional choice to time the annual redistribution ritual to this window inherits the cultural resonances of all four events without manufacturing a new ritual surface. The essay specifies the **Twelve Days of Christmas** as the canonical fulfillment-cycle structure within which the Aquarian Pool empties (gradually, throughout the twelve days, rather than instantaneously on either Christmas date), the **Christian-Buddhist resonance** at the doctrinal layer (the theme of universal redistribution, *jubilee*, *dāna*, the cancellation of debt), the **Cambodian civic resonance** at the institutional layer (a Cambodian-headquartered institution that aligns its central annual ritual with the Cambodian Victory over Genocide Day reinforces its cultural rooting), and the **incidental founder-birthday alignment** that is true (the founder's birthday is January 7, 1985) but explicitly *not* the load-bearing reason for the choice. The essay closes with reflection on what civilizational-scale rituals require structurally (predictable annual rhythm; doctrinal substance; civic resonance; institutional accountability) and how the Christmas-Jubilee timing satisfies each requirement at minimum institutional cost.

**Keywords:** annual ritual design, Twelve Days of Christmas, Orthodox Christmas, Cambodian Victory over Genocide Day, redistribution timing, jubilee tradition, *dāna* tradition, civilizational-scale institutional design, defensive publication.

---

## 1. Introduction

The question of *when* an institution performs its central annual ritual is not incidental. The timing is institutional substance: it shapes participant expectations, ritualizes preparation, anchors cultural memory, and aligns the institution with the cultural rhythms participants already inhabit. Civilizations have long understood this; the Jewish *Yom Kippur*, the Christian Easter, the Hindu Diwali, the Cambodian Khmer New Year (April), the Islamic Eid al-Fitr — each is a calendar-anchored ritual whose timing carries institutional substance independent of the ritual's content.

The institution this paper serves is HeartBank, whose central annual ritual is the *emptying of the Aquarian Pool*: the institutional pool from which aura-weighted redistributions flow to participating families annually. The question is when, in the annual calendar, this emptying should occur. This essay argues that the convergence of four annually-recurring liberation-and-redistribution events on a single twelve-day window — **December 25 through January 7** — makes that window the maximally-resonant annual anchor, and that the institution's choice to time its central ritual to this window is institutional substance worth articulating explicitly.

> *Connection to the unified mission frame: HeartBank's mission is the restoration of humanity to the middle way — the optimal condition for awakening that modernity has systematically pushed away from at population scale. A planetary institution whose mission spans multiple cultural contexts requires a central ritual whose timing is resonant in those contexts without requiring imposition of an unfamiliar calendar. The Christmas-Jubilee timing inherits the Christian-Western, Christian-Eastern, and Cambodian-civic resonances simultaneously; the institutional choice extends to the Buddhist-jubilee resonance at the doctrinal layer; the resulting four-fold resonance is achieved at minimum institutional cost and without manufacturing an artificial ritual surface.*

The essay proceeds as follows. §2 specifies the four events whose convergence makes the window resonant. §3 specifies the Twelve Days of Christmas as the canonical fulfillment-cycle structure. §4 articulates the doctrinal-resonance argument. §5 specifies the Cambodian civic resonance. §6 addresses the founder-birthday alignment honestly. §7 articulates what civilizational-scale rituals require structurally and how the timing satisfies each requirement. §8 closes.

---

## 2. The four converging events

### 2.1 Western Christmas (December 25)

The canonical Christian annual ritual of generosity, gift-giving, and family reconciliation. The December 25 date is the Gregorian-calendar fixing of the Christian Nativity celebration; it has been the most widely observed calendar date for ritualized generosity in the Western world for approximately seventeen hundred years. The cultural infrastructure surrounding the date (the gift-giving tradition; the family-gathering convention; the year-end giving cycle that the date anchors for many charitable institutions) is institutional substance the timing inherits.

### 2.2 Orthodox Christmas (January 7)

The Julian-calendar celebration of the same Christian Nativity, observed by Eastern Orthodox communities (Russian, Greek, Serbian, Coptic, Ethiopian, Armenian, and others) and several Eastern-rite Catholic communities. The January 7 date carries the same theological substance as the December 25 date; the calendrical difference is a function of the Gregorian / Julian calendar divergence and does not reflect doctrinal difference about what is being celebrated. For institutions operating cross-tradition, the two-date pair (rather than either single date) is the appropriate ritual surface.

### 2.3 Cambodia's Victory over Genocide Day (January 7)

The Cambodian national holiday commemorating the liberation of Phnom Penh from the Khmer Rouge regime on January 7, 1979. The most consequential civic liberation event in Cambodian modern history; the institutional rebirth of the country after the genocide. For a Cambodian-headquartered institution, the date carries civic resonance that no other date in the Cambodian annual calendar matches.

### 2.4 The Aquarian Pool's annual emptying (December 25 → January 7)

The HeartBank institutional redistribution ritual. The Aquarian Pool empties gradually across the twelve-day window, culminating on January 7. The institutional design choice is to align the ritual's structure with the Christian Twelve Days of Christmas (§3) so that the ritual unfolds over the same window as the cultural-religious events whose resonance it inherits.

### 2.5 The convergence as structural aptness

The convergence is not metaphysical or providential; the four events have independent historical causation. The argument is *structural*: the institutional choice to align the ritual window with the existing cultural-religious-civic events inherits their resonances without manufacturing a new ritual surface. An alternative timing (say, a fall-equinox anchor; a summer-solstice anchor; an arbitrary date chosen for operational convenience) would require the institution to *construct* the cultural resonance from scratch. The Christmas-Jubilee timing inherits it.

---

## 3. The Twelve Days of Christmas as fulfillment-cycle structure

### 3.1 The Christian liturgical tradition

The Twelve Days of Christmas is the traditional Christian liturgical period running from Christmas Day (December 25) through Epiphany (January 6), with the Orthodox observance extending an additional day to January 7. The period is, in many Christian traditions, the central festal cycle of the year; it carries the theological substance of *Incarnation* (the divine entering the human world) and the practical substance of extended family gathering, gift exchange, and communal celebration.

### 3.2 The HeartBank adaptation

The Aquarian Pool's emptying is structured as a *gradual fulfillment cycle* across the twelve days, culminating on January 7. The institutional design choice is intentional: a single-day emptying (on either December 25 or January 7) would be operationally simpler but would forfeit the *anticipation, gradual fulfillment, and culminating arrival* structure that the Twelve Days tradition provides. The gradual emptying mirrors the canonical festal cycle's *cumulative arrival*.

### 3.3 The doctrinal-resonance specification

The Twelve Days carry the *Incarnation* doctrinal substance in the Christian tradition; the HeartBank adaptation carries an analogous doctrinal substance: *the institutional substance becoming participant-substance* through the redistribution. The Aquarian Pool (which has accumulated through the year via institutional flows) becomes participant-resource (in the form of family-kitty disbursements) through the twelve-day window. The structural analogy with Incarnation is not opportunistic; it is the doctrinal substance the timing carries.

### 3.4 The pacing as institutional discipline

The pacing of the twelve-day emptying is governed by Miss Aquarius's autonomous logic per pre-committed rules (per the *Non-Bank Pass-Through* paper's smart-contract specification). The pacing is intentionally rule-bound rather than discretionary; the institutional discipline is to let the annual cycle proceed automatically rather than allowing the institutional officers to time-shift disbursements for any reason.

---

## 4. Doctrinal resonance

### 4.1 The Christian jubilee tradition

The Christian jubilee tradition (rooted in Leviticus 25 and developed in Catholic tradition through the Holy Years declared periodically by the Vatican) is the theological substance of *periodic-redistribution-as-divine-mandate*. The jubilee originally called for, every fifty years, the cancellation of debts, the freeing of indentured servants, the restoration of ancestral lands. The institutional HeartBank Pool-emptying is a contemporary jubilee at annual rather than fifty-year cadence; the doctrinal substance is the same (*the periodic mandatory redistribution*).

### 4.2 The Buddhist *dāna* tradition

The Buddhist *dāna* tradition (the foundational gift-economy substrate of the Theravāda monastic order) is the theological substance of *gift-as-the-foundational-economic-act*. The institutional HeartBank Pool-emptying is a contemporary *dāna* ritual; the doctrinal substance is the same (*the foundational substance of the institutional economy is the gift*).

### 4.3 The cross-tradition resonance

The Christmas-Jubilee timing carries the Christian jubilee resonance (through the Twelve Days liturgical cycle) and the Buddhist *dāna* resonance (through the institutional substance of the ritual) simultaneously. The cross-tradition resonance is not opportunistic syncretism; it is the convergence of two contemplative traditions on the same structural insight (periodic generous redistribution as the foundational economic act).

### 4.4 Other tradition resonances

The Islamic *zakat* tradition (annual mandatory charity) shares the periodic-redistribution structural insight, though typically at the Ramadan-cycle calendar timing rather than the Christmas-cycle timing. The Jewish *Yom Kippur* tradition (annual day of repentance and reconciliation) shares the periodic-reset structural insight at fall calendar timing. The Hindu *Diwali* tradition (annual festival of lights including ritualized giving) shares the festal-cycle structure at autumn timing. The HeartBank institution operates the Christmas-Jubilee timing because of the specific convergence of the four events specified; institutions in other cultural contexts may appropriately adopt different timings with similar structural substance.

---

## 5. Cambodian civic resonance

### 5.1 The Victory over Genocide Day substance

January 7 is the date Phnom Penh was liberated from the Khmer Rouge in 1979. The Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979) was responsible for the deaths of approximately one-quarter of the Cambodian population through execution, starvation, and disease; the regime systematically targeted intellectuals, monastics, ethnic minorities, and urban populations. The liberation date marks the institutional rebirth of Cambodian civic society after the most consequential civilizational catastrophe in the country's modern history.

### 5.2 The institutional alignment

A Cambodian-headquartered institution whose central annual ritual aligns with the Cambodian Victory over Genocide Day signals — without requiring explicit articulation — that the institution carries the country's civic memory at its core ritual layer. The signal is institutional substance the timing makes available.

### 5.3 The diaspora resonance

The Khmer diaspora — particularly in California, Massachusetts, France, and Australia — carries the Victory over Genocide Day observance through community institutions, family commemoration, and civic events. The institutional alignment with the date extends the institution's resonance into the diaspora communities the institution serves.

### 5.4 The dual-resonance choice

The Christmas-Jubilee timing carries both the Christian-religious resonance and the Cambodian-civic resonance simultaneously, with no need to choose between them. The dual-resonance is the institutional substance the convergence makes available.

---

## 6. The founder-birthday alignment

### 6.1 The fact

The founder's birthday is January 7, 1985. The birthday-alignment is true.

### 6.2 The honest framing

The birthday alignment is *not* the load-bearing reason for the timing choice. The institutional discipline requires that the timing be defensible on its own structural merits (the four-event convergence specified in §2; the Twelve Days fulfillment cycle in §3; the doctrinal resonance in §4; the Cambodian civic resonance in §5) without relying on the founder-personal resonance. The institutional ritual's timing must outlast the founder; it cannot rest on his calendar.

### 6.3 What the alignment does mean

The alignment means that the founder's personal calendar happens to align with the institutional calendar, which is meaningful in the personal sense (the founder is born on the date the institution he founds will eventually anchor its annual ritual to) but does not transfer to institutional warrant for the timing choice. The institutional warrant comes from §2–§5, not from §6.

### 6.4 The institutional-discipline reason for explicit treatment

The founder-birthday alignment is named explicitly in this essay precisely so that future readers, encountering the timing choice and noticing the alignment, can verify that the institutional warrant is articulated independently. An institution whose central ritual aligns with the founder's birthday would be vulnerable to the criticism that the ritual is *about* the founder; the explicit articulation that the warrant is independent forecloses that criticism by demonstrating the structural reasoning.

---

## 7. What civilizational-scale rituals require structurally

The Christmas-Jubilee timing satisfies the four structural requirements of civilizational-scale rituals.

### 7.1 Predictable annual rhythm

A civilizational ritual must occur on a predictable annual cadence so that participants can prepare, anticipate, and integrate the ritual into their own calendar rhythms. The Christmas-Jubilee timing's twelve-day window is predictable, calendrically fixed, and integrated into participants' existing year-end calendar patterns (year-end-giving cycles; holiday family gatherings; year-end financial planning).

### 7.2 Doctrinal substance

A civilizational ritual must carry doctrinal substance — a meaningful institutional claim about what the ritual is *for*. The Christmas-Jubilee timing carries the Christian jubilee and Buddhist *dāna* substances (§4); the institutional substance (the Aquarian Pool emptying as institutional substance becoming participant substance) is doctrinally articulated.

### 7.3 Civic resonance

A civilizational ritual must resonate with the civic memory of the contexts the institution operates in. The Christmas-Jubilee timing carries the Western and Eastern Christian civic resonance and the Cambodian civic resonance simultaneously (§5).

### 7.4 Institutional accountability

A civilizational ritual must be *visible*; participants must be able to verify that the ritual was performed as specified, with what flows and what disbursements. The Aquarian Pool's smart-contract implementation makes the emptying public-ledger-visible per the *Non-Bank Pass-Through* paper's specification; participants and observers can verify the ritual's execution against the pre-committed rules.

### 7.5 The minimal-cost satisfaction

The Christmas-Jubilee timing satisfies all four requirements at minimum institutional cost. The institution does not need to manufacture cultural resonance; it inherits Christian, Buddhist, and Cambodian resonances simultaneously. The institution does not need to invent a fulfillment-cycle structure; it adopts the Twelve Days tradition. The institution does not need to construct civic alignment; the convergence with Cambodian Victory over Genocide Day provides it. The minimal-cost satisfaction is the institutional efficiency the timing choice produces.

---

## 8. Conclusion

The Christmas-Jubilee timing is offered as a defensive publication so that other institutions designing civilizational-scale annual rituals can adopt the analytical pattern (identify the calendar convergences that make a window resonant; adopt the fulfillment-cycle structure that culminates rather than punctuates; honor the doctrinal substance the timing carries; preserve institutional accountability through public-ledger visibility) without patent risk.

For institutions in other cultural contexts where the December 25 → January 7 window does not carry the convergent resonances specified, the pattern is the same but the specific calendar choice differs. Institutions in primarily Islamic contexts may anchor to the Ramadan / Eid al-Fitr cycle; institutions in primarily Hindu contexts may anchor to the Diwali cycle; institutions in primarily Jewish contexts may anchor to the High Holy Days cycle. The analytical discipline (identify the calendar resonances; adopt the fulfillment-cycle structure; honor the doctrinal substance) translates; the specific calendar choice does not.

The author and HeartBank® will not seek patent on this analytical pattern. The work is offered to the commons under CC0 in the spirit of *dāna*, that other institutions building civilizational-scale rituals may adopt and adapt.

---

documents.title: Circulation Sports: A Category That Already Had Members and No Name
documents.subtitle: The Three Properties, the Conversion Operator, the Drill/Sport Differentia, and a Census of the Warm-Ups That Were Already Doing It
documents.text:
> *Draft notes for the editor:* this paper claims a **taxonomy**, not a mechanism. There is no patentable machinery here and therefore no defensive clock; it is published early for a different reason, which is that a category is defined by whoever specifies it first, and a category specified badly by an incumbent is harder to repair than one specified openly now. Its sibling *The Sport That Says Your Name* (2026-07-23) owns the **caller mechanism** of B-Sey™; the present paper owns the **class of sports** that mechanism instantiates, and takes care to claim nothing that belongs to the members it did not create. The category name is dedicated to the public domain and will never be registered as a mark — the same split already applied to `sey` (free) and B-Sey™ (the mark). **One pre-registration in this paper has already been run, and it returned a partial null against the authors' own prediction; §8 reports the failure before it reports what survives.** The prior-art clock, such as it is, starts at this markdown push.

---

## Abstract

Some sports score the moment an exchange **ends** — the ball goes in, the rally dies, the opponent fails. Some score the moment an exchange **continues**. The second kind has existed for at least fourteen centuries, has members on four continents, and has never had a name or a specification. This paper supplies both.

A **circulation sport** is defined here by three properties held together: it scores the **completed transfer** rather than the termination; it **reaches every participant**, as a rule that makes skipping someone impossible rather than merely impolite; and it **accumulates to no one**, keeping no individual record. The three are not a feature list drawn from one game. They are a transformation rule, and the paper states it as a three-step **conversion operator** that can be applied by someone else to a sport we have never played — with worked conversions of basketball, volleyball, soccer, and tennis, and with the boundary drawn as carefully as the interior (Ultimate Frisbee is out; the rondo fails on reach; golf is the antipode). Of the three, one carries a precondition that is not a choice at all: below three participants a completed transfer is indistinguishable from a return, so **three is the smallest number at which "forward" is defined** — a result belonging to Lévi-Strauss, to the kula literature, and to the evolutionary work on upstream reciprocity, which §2.5 cites rather than claims.

Three findings drove the paper and none of them flatter it. **First**, the operator is not new, because it has already been run — in the opposite direction, in public, with a date and a name attached. The Malay circle game *sepak raga bulatan*, in which players take turns keeping a rattan ball aloft, was converted into a competitive net sport in February 1945 by Hamid Maidin, and standardized as *sepak takraw* at a five-nation meeting in Kuala Lumpur in 1960. What this paper specifies is the **inverse of a documented historical operation**, not a novelty. **Second**, applying the operator to any classic sport tends to produce something that already exists as that sport's own warm-up — pepper, mini-tennis, the rondo, passing lines — which makes the category an empirical question with a natural experiment already running in every youth league on earth, rather than a proposal. **Third**, the authors pre-registered a census of those warm-ups (P-CS5) predicting that reach guarantees would prove **rare**, and then ran it. **They are not rare.** Reach guarantees are common, in at least four distinct architectures. The pre-registered claim is falsified and is reported as falsified. What survives is narrower, was arrived at after the data, and is labeled accordingly: every attested reach guarantee **purchases reach with predictability** — a queue, a fixed role rotation, or a memorized pattern all tell you when your turn is coming — and reach whose order stays unpredictable across unbounded play remains unattested. That gap, not reach itself, is where the sibling paper's caller mechanism sits.

The paper also states the differentia that decides whether any of this describes **sports** at all: *a sport owns its own ending; a drill is stopped from outside.* Within the genus of physical skilled activity that separation is necessary though not sufficient, and it supplies the category's own life-or-death test — if converted forms are only ever played instrumentally, as warm-ups and means to the competitive game, then this is a taxonomy of drills wearing a taxonomy of sports. **Five predictions are pre-registered with instruments and nulls, one of them already resolved against us**, together with an annual review date, and the whole set is stated against the base rate it must beat: cooperative sport has been tried as an organized movement, had a real decade, and did not displace competitive sport. One distinction is offered as the reason this is not that movement returning: **a cooperative game removes the opponent; a circulation sport keeps the opponent and changes what counts as a point.**

**Keywords:** sport taxonomy, circulation sport, cooperative games, conversion operator, kemari, chinlone, sepak raga, sepak takraw, rondo, warm-up drills, equal participation, non-accumulation, drill versus sport, pre-registration, defensive publication.

---

## Prior-Art and Non-Assertion Statement

This document and its contents are dedicated to the public domain under the Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication. The authors and HeartBank® will not seek patent, trademark, or any other exclusive right on the category defined herein, in any jurisdiction, at any time. **The term "circulation sport" is coined here and freed here, deliberately and permanently.** A category that one party owns is a category nobody adopts, and the value of this work — if it has any — is entirely in other people applying it to sports we will never play. The institution's own product mark (B-Sey™/℠) is unaffected and is not the subject of this paper; the split between a freed idea and a held mark is the same one already applied to the Khmer word `sey`, which is free, and B-Sey™, which is not.

Terms coined and freed with this paper: **circulation sport**, **the conversion operator**, **the reach guarantee**, **the predictability price**, **the drill/sport differentia** as stated in §9, and **the warm-up census** as a survey method.

Terms inherited from this corpus's earlier publications are **cited, not re-claimed**: *equal-yet-random distribution*, *the caller mechanism*, *the cannot-target-weakness property*, *the dyadic scoring unit*, *start-line handicap*, and *the play/currency wall* all belong to *The Sport That Says Your Name* (2026-07-23) and are dedicated there.

**Most of this paper's subject matter is not ours and is not claimed.** Kemari, chinlone, sepak raga, jianzi, footbag, and *sey* itself are living or historical traditions belonging to the communities that carry them. Terry Orlick's cooperative-games canon and the New Games Movement are prior art of the most direct kind, and are treated in §10 as the position this paper has to answer rather than as background. Every warm-up drill surveyed in §8 was invented by coaches whose names are mostly unrecorded. **The contribution claimed here is a definition, a procedure, a boundary, a falsification test, and one census — nothing more.**

---

## 1 · Why an Institution Building a Gratitude Ledger Is Writing About Sport

This paper belongs to a body of work on **reciprocity infrastructure** — systems in which value moves because someone gave, rather than because someone paid. That work has a physical problem it cannot solve on a screen. Giving, at the scale where it changes a person, is learned in bodies and in groups, early, and mostly through play. A child who has never been passed to has not learned a fact about passing; they have learned a fact about themselves.

The institution's operative unit is a **gift given forward**: something received and passed on, rather than received and returned. Sport is where that unit either exists in a person's motor memory or does not. So the question this paper asks is narrow and practical. *Which sports are built out of the give-forward unit, and is there a procedure for building more of them?*

It turns out that some are, that they are old, that they are scattered across cultures that never compared notes, and that nobody had collected them. That is the whole occasion for this paper. **We are not proposing that competitive sport is a mistake.** Competition is one of the great engines of skill, and this paper's central distinction (§10) exists precisely to keep the opponent rather than remove them. What is proposed is that a second family of sports exists alongside the competitive one, that it has been under-specified to the point of invisibility, and that its members would be easier to make on purpose if somebody wrote down how.

A note on tone that the rest of the paper tries to keep. It is easy to write about non-competitive play by cataloguing what competitive play does to children. That register is available and this paper declines it. **The claim here is about what circulation *is*, never about what competition *lacks*** — partly because the second claim is not one the evidence supports, and partly because a taxonomy written as an indictment gets read as an indictment and not as a taxonomy.

---

## 2 · The Category, Specified

A category needs a transformation rule rather than a list of one game's features, or it is a description of that game with ambitions. Three properties, held **together**:

### 2.1 It scores the completed transfer, not the termination

In classic competitive sport the scoring event is an **ending**. The ball goes through the hoop; the rally dies on your opponent's side; the puck crosses the line. Value is created by *ending the exchange in your favor*. The transfer — the pass, the assist, the set, the feed — is instrumental to that ending and is recorded, if at all, as a supporting statistic.

In a circulation sport the polarity is inverted. **Value is created by the exchange continuing.** The scoring unit is a transfer that arrived: a pass completed, a rally sustained, a ball kept up. The termination still exists and is still necessary — a rally must eventually end — but it is demoted to a non-scoring event, and in the sharper members it is the thing that *stops* the count rather than the thing that increments it.

### 2.2 It reaches everyone

This property is not a fairness guard bolted onto a game. It is what the word *circulation* means. A circulatory system that skips an organ is not a circulatory system operating imperfectly; it is a pathology with a name. Blood that does not reach the extremities is the definition of circulatory failure.

So the requirement is strict, and the strictness is the point: **skipping a participant must be impossible as a move, not merely discouraged as a habit.** A rule that says "try to include everyone" does not satisfy this. A bonus for including everyone does not satisfy it either — §8 finds exactly such a bonus in the wild and classifies it as a near-miss. What satisfies it is a distribution rule that removes the choice: a mandatory rotation, a called receiver, a round that is not complete until every participant has received.

### 2.3 It accumulates to no one

Classic sports are, among other things, **archives of individual accumulation**. Career goals, batting averages, personal bests, the ranked ladder, the hall of fame. The archive is not incidental to those sports; for many participants it is the point, and it is a large part of what makes elite competition legible and worth watching.

A circulation sport refuses the archive. No player statistics, ever. Counts that run down rather than up, or streaks that always eventually die, or records that belong to the circle rather than to any person in it. The test is simple: **after the session, is there any number attached to an individual that persists?** If yes, the property fails.

### 2.4 The three together, and why the conjunction matters

Each property alone is common. Together they are not.

```
     PROPERTY (i)              PROPERTY (ii)             PROPERTY (iii)
   transfer scores            reaches everyone          nothing accrues
         |                          |                          |
   "the pass IS            "you cannot skip me"      "no record with a
    the point"                                        name on it"
         |                          |                          |
         +--------------------------+--------------------------+
                                    |
                          A CIRCULATION SPORT
                    (all three, simultaneously, as RULES
                     rather than as etiquette or coaching)
```

The conjunction is what does the work, and §6 and §8 are both exercises in showing how many familiar activities hold two of the three.

### 2.5 The minimum arity: why the circle is three

*Added 2026-08-22. The three properties above are stated as design choices, and two of them are. This section reports the one that is not — and it is a result the paper stands on rather than announces, because it belongs to anthropology and to evolutionary dynamics and has for decades.*

The question arrived from the wrong end. Asked whether the sibling paper's game could be played by two people as a simple name courtesy — one says the other's name, the other says it back — we answered no, and then had to work out why, because the honest first answer was only that it did not feel like the game. Two people can pass a ball, sustain a rally, take turns, and enjoy an hour of it. What two people cannot do is **circulate**.

**At N = 2, every pass forward is a pass back.** The second player has exactly one address to send the thing to, and it is the address it came from. Forward and back are the same edge. Which means the unit this category is built on — a transfer that continues *away* from its source — has no way to distinguish itself from the unit it is defined against, a transfer that returns. What a dyad has is reciprocation, and reciprocation is not a defective circulation; it is a different and entirely respectable thing, with its own long literature and its own social work to do.

At N = 3 the two motions come apart for the first time. A passes to B, and B's forward option (C) is now a different edge from B's return option (A). The choice exists, and so the category does.

```
            N = 2                                  N = 3

          A ─────► B                             A ─────► B
          ▲        │                             ▲        │
          └────────┘                             │        ▼
                                                 └─────── C

     forward and back are               forward (A→B→C→A) and back (B→A)
     THE SAME EDGE                      are DIFFERENT EDGES
```

**Three is therefore the smallest number at which "forward" is defined.** Not the smallest number at which the game is fun, or fair, or worth organizing — those are different questions with different answers. It is the smallest number at which the category's own unit is distinguishable from its complement, which makes it a fact about the definition in §2, not a fact about anybody's product.

**The result is not ours, and it has been settled three times in three literatures.** In kinship theory, Lévi-Strauss's *Les structures élémentaires de la parenté* (1949; English: *The Elementary Structures of Kinship*, Beacon Press, 1969) draws exactly this line, calling the two-group case **restricted exchange** — direct and immediate, A and B trading with each other — and the three-or-more case **generalized exchange**, in which A gives to B, B to C, and C back to A, delayed and indirect, and capable of integrating an indefinite number of groups precisely because it is not a swap. In economic anthropology the attested instance is the Trobriand **kula** ring (Malinowski, *Argonauts of the Western Pacific*, 1922), a circuit of many islands in which valuables travel in one direction and are never traded back along the edge they arrived on. And in evolutionary dynamics the same threshold is stated formally: **upstream reciprocity** — help someone because someone helped you — is distinguished from direct reciprocity by exactly this arithmetic, since the shortest possible cycle of indirect reciprocity is three players, a two-player cycle being direct reciprocity by definition (Boyd & Richerson, "The evolution of indirect reciprocity," *Social Networks* 11(3), 1989; Nowak & Roch, "Upstream reciprocity and the evolution of gratitude," *Proc. R. Soc. B* 274(1610): 605–610, 2007).

That last paper's title should be read as the caution it is. The mechanism this institution builds on has been modelled, named, and published under the word *gratitude* for nearly twenty years. **We are late to it, and the correct posture is grounding, not discovery** — the same posture §8 arrived at the hard way when the census returned a null against our own prediction.

**One conflation to avoid, because we nearly committed it.** Sahlins's celebrated triad — **generalized**, **balanced**, and **negative** reciprocity ("On the Sociology of Primitive Exchange," in Banton, ed., *The Relevance of Models for Social Anthropology*, ASA Monographs 1, Tavistock, 1965; reprinted in *Stone Age Economics*, 1972) — sorts exchange by **social distance and the expectation of return**, not by the number of parties. Sahlins's *generalized reciprocity* means open-ended giving among close kin with no reckoning of equivalence; Lévi-Strauss's *generalized exchange* means a cycle of three or more. **The two share a word and not a claim**, and a paper that cited them as one argument would be citing prior art wrongly, which is worse than not citing it at all.

**What this does for the definition in §2.** It splits the three properties by their modal status, which they did not previously have. Properties (ii) *reaches everyone* and (iii) *accumulates to no one* remain design choices: a designer could build a transfer-scoring sport without either, and §6 and §8 are full of activities that do. Property (i) — scoring the completed transfer — is a design choice too, but it carries a **precondition** that is not: below three participants there is no completed transfer distinguishable from a return, and the property cannot be satisfied because it cannot be stated. The definition thus rests on one forced floor and two chosen walls, and saying so makes the category slightly smaller and considerably more honest than it was when all three properties looked alike.

**What is deliberately not claimed here.** Not that three is a good size — it is a floor and a poor ceiling, and most attested members of the category run much larger. Not that the floor implies any particular quorum for any particular product, which is a design question this paper does not touch. And not, emphatically, that the arithmetic makes a dyad's kindnesses lesser: a couple passing a thing back and forth is doing something the human record values enormously, and the only claim made is that it is not the thing this paper is naming.

---

## 3 · The Members That Already Existed

The single most important sentence in this paper is that **we did not invent this category, and its best members predate us by centuries.** A reader who knows the field and finds these uncited would be right to stop reading.

**Kemari (蹴鞠, Japan).** A court football of the Heian (794–1185) and Kamakura (1185–1333) periods, introduced from China before the seventh century; one of the earliest references places a game at Hōkōji in Nara in 644 CE. Eight participants stand in a circle and keep a ball aloft with the feet, passing it to one another with control and precision. Its competitive nature was deliberately shed: the goal is to keep the ball from touching the ground, together, for as long as possible. Its rules were standardized from the thirteenth century. It declined after the Meiji Restoration and survives because a preservation society was founded in 1903 with a donation from Emperor Meiji. **Kemari satisfies all three properties and has done so for fourteen hundred years.**

**Chinlone (ခြင်းလုံး, Myanmar).** The national sport of Myanmar, played by six people as one team with a hand-woven rattan ball. There is no opposing team, no goalposts, and no formal rule about winning or losing. Success is measured by how long the ball stays airborne and how gracefully each touch is executed; one player occupies the center of the circle. It is commonly described as closer to an art than to a contest.

**Sepak raga bulatan (Malay Archipelago).** The circle form, considered the original variant: players stand in a ring and keep a woven rattan ball aloft with feet, knees, chest, and head, **taking turns**, emphasizing skill and endurance rather than competition. Its documented history reaches the Malacca Sultanate of the fifteenth century, and the *Sejarah Melayu* records a game in which a prince was struck by the ball, triggering a political conflict — which is to say the game was consequential enough to appear in a court chronicle.

**Jianzi (毽子, China), footbag circles, and keepie-uppie** are the same shape at smaller scale and with different objects.

**Sey (សី, Cambodia)** is the game this institution's own sport descends from — a folk game played at dusk, inherited rather than invented, in which a circle keeps an object alive together. Its treatment as a *design* rather than an inheritance would be the same error this section exists to prevent.

> The lineage is worth stating plainly because of where it sits: **four of the strongest members of this category are Asian circle games, three of them Southeast Asian, and the specification is being written by a Cambodian institution about a Khmer game.** That is a reason for care rather than for pride. The tradition is older than the theory and does not require it.

---

## 4 · The Conversion Has Already Been Run — In the Other Direction

This is the finding that most changed the paper, and it removes the last of its claim to novelty in a way that makes it stronger rather than weaker.

The Malay circle game did not merely coexist with a competitive net sport. **It was converted into one, by a named person, on a date.** In February 1945, Hamid Maidin introduced a net (*jaring*) and rules adapted from volleyball, inviting Mohamad Abdul Rahman — described as the best player of the circle game — and Syed Yaacob to try it. In 1960, delegates from Malaya, Singapore, Indonesia, Laos, and Thailand met in Kuala Lumpur, standardized the rules, and adopted the name **sepak takraw**, under which the sport is now governed internationally.

Read against §2, that history is a documented, attributed run of the conversion operator **in reverse**:

```
   sepak raga bulatan                        sepak takraw
   -------------------                       ------------
   circle, turn-taking            Feb 1945   two sides, a net
   keep it aloft together         --------→  end the rally on their side
   no score, no sides             (jaring)   points, sets, matches
   reaches everyone                  1960     targeting the weak side is
   accumulates to no one           (naming)   a legitimate tactic
                                              individual and team records

   THREE PROPERTIES HELD                     THREE PROPERTIES RELEASED
```

Three consequences follow, and all three are load-bearing.

**The operator is real.** It is not a theoretical construct invented to justify one product. A human being ran it in one direction in 1945, deliberately, with a design intent that is legible eighty years later. A procedure that has been executed once has a much stronger claim to being a procedure than one that has only been described.

**The direction is a choice, not a gradient.** It is tempting to narrate sport as evolving from folk play toward formal competition, with circulation as the primitive stage. The 1945 conversion is better read as an *option that was taken*: the circle form did not die of natural causes, and in fact it did not die at all — chinlone and kemari are both alive, and the *bulatan* form persists. Somebody added a net because a net was useful for organizing tournaments. The inverse operation is equally available and has simply never been written down.

**Our contribution shrinks to the right size.** This paper does not propose a new kind of sport. It specifies the inverse of an operation that has been performed, names the class the pre-conversion games belong to, and asks whether the inverse can be run deliberately. That is a smaller claim than "a new category of sport," and it is the one the evidence supports.

---

## 5 · The Conversion Operator

A named operator that is never written is a promise, not a contribution. Here it is as a procedure, stated so that someone who has never spoken to us can apply it to a sport we have never played.

> **(i) RE-SEAT THE SCORING UNIT.** Find the sport's existing *transfer* event — pass, assist, set, feed, handoff, rally stroke — and make that the point. Demote the termination to a non-scoring necessity.
>
> **(ii) GUARANTEE REACH.** Add a distribution rule that makes skipping or targeting a participant impossible *as a move*: a called receiver, a mandatory rotation, an all-must-touch requirement, or a round that does not close until everyone has received.
>
> **(iii) DELETE ACCUMULATION.** No individual statistics, ever. Records belong to the unit. Counts run down, or die, or are not kept.

### 5.1 Worked conversions

The operator must produce **playable games** or the category is one sport wearing a taxonomy. Four worked examples, chosen because they span net, invasion, and racket sports:

| Sport | (i) transfer as the point | (ii) reach | (iii) no accumulation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Basketball** | the **assist** scores; a basket without a preceding pass is worth nothing | all five must touch before a shot may be taken | team streak only; no box score |
| **Volleyball** | completed **three-touch sequences across the net**, counted by both sides together | rotation already exists; extend it to guaranteed contacts | the rally that never dies is the record |
| **Soccer** | possession-chain length; a goal counts only after **N unique touchers** | the N-unique-touchers requirement *is* the reach rule | chain records, never scorers |
| **Tennis** | **rally count** | strict alternation is inherent to the sport | the rally dies and nothing carries |

An honest note about these outputs, which §7 will develop: **none of them are inventions.** Every one already exists somewhere as a warm-up, a youth rule, or a coaching game. That is not an embarrassment for the operator; it is the strongest available evidence that the operator describes something real. *The operator's value is that it explains what these have in common, not that it produces novelties.*

### 5.2 The scope guard

The operator is a **corpus contribution and not a product roadmap.** This institution's own sport is deliberately scoped to the first fifteen minutes of a practice and is explicitly not a platform for all sports. Publishing a general conversion procedure while keeping the product narrow is the same split applied elsewhere in this corpus: **keep the product narrow and the idea broad.** Other people convert their own sports; that is the intended outcome, and the CC0 dedication exists to make it frictionless.

---

## 6 · The Negative Space

A category that admits everything explains nothing. The boundary is drawn here with more care than the interior, because the boundary is where the definition is tested.

**Ultimate Frisbee — OUT, and it is the cleanest near-miss.** Ultimate's Spirit of the Game is a genuine and admirable normative achievement, and it is *governance*: it regulates conduct, self-officiating, and dispute resolution. It does not touch the scoring unit. A point in Ultimate is scored by catching the disc in the end zone — a termination — and defense consists of preventing that. Ultimate is a well-governed competitive sport, which is a fine thing to be. **Its exclusion is what proves the category is about the scoring unit rather than about niceness**, and any definition that lets Ultimate in has quietly become a definition of good sportsmanship.

**Relay races — PARTIAL.** The transfer is real and ceremonial (the baton exchange is the most transfer-centric moment in track), and reach is guaranteed by the structure. But the scoring event is a finish line, and results accumulate to teams and to individuals in the record book. Two of three.

**Rondo / piggy-in-the-middle — FAILS (ii), and instructively.** The rondo scores consecutive completed passes, which is property (i) done well and is precisely why it is such a beloved warm-up. But it has a **designated loser** in the middle, and the defender who wins the ball changes places with the player who lost it. Targeting the weakest passer is not a violation of the rondo; it is how you get out of the middle. *Reach is not merely unguaranteed here — its opposite is the objective.*

**Shooting lines and batting practice — FAIL (i) and (iii).** There is no transfer at all, and makes are counted individually. Pure individual accumulation in a warm-up costume.

**Cooperative board games — OUT.** No circulating physical token and no bodies; whatever they are, they are not sports, and stretching the category to reach them would cost the definition its shape.

**Golf — THE ANTIPODE.** No transfer, complete individual accumulation, and a scoring unit that is a termination repeated. Golf is useful precisely as the category's polar opposite — and note the one circulatory organ it does contain: **the handicap**, a mechanism whose whole purpose is to let unequal players share a game, which is the reach property arriving through the back door of a sport built without it.

---

## 7 · The Discovery: Every Classic Sport Already Contains Its Circulatory Form

Applying the operator turned up something better than the operator.

**Its outputs already exist, scattered, as warm-ups and youth rules.** Pepper. Mini-tennis rallies. Passing lines. The rondo. Five-passes-before-you-shoot. Keep-it-up. The butterfly drill. Nobody appears to have noticed that these are one family — that the volleyball coach and the soccer coach and the tennis coach have each independently built the circulatory form of their own sport, called it a warm-up, and used it for fifteen minutes before playing the real one.

This matters more than the taxonomy does, because it converts the category from a proposal into an **empirical question with a natural experiment already running in every youth league on earth.** We do not have to argue that circulation sports would be enjoyable. We can go and look at whether the ones that already exist are.

It also promotes what had been the weakest of the founder's four predictions into the strongest. *"Warming up with sey gets extended longer and longer"* had been filed as a test of whether a drill is fun. If warm-ups **are** the circulatory forms of their own sports, then a warm-up that keeps getting extended is **the circulatory form eating the competitive one, measured inside a single session** — the category thesis in miniature, at the smallest scale at which it could possibly be observed.

## 8 · The Census (P-CS5), Run — And the Null That Fired

### 8.1 What was pre-registered, and when

On **2026-08-05**, before any survey was conducted, the authors registered the following prediction:

> **P-CS5 — the warm-up census.** Survey what mainstream sports do in warm-ups and score each format against the three properties. *Predicted shape: properties (i) transfer-as-the-point and (iii) no-accumulation are **common**; property (ii) **reach** is **rare** — and (ii) is where the sibling paper's entire contribution sits.* **Stated null: if reach guarantees turn out to be common, the uniqueness claim weakens materially.**

The census was run on **2026-08-07** as a desk survey of published coaching materials across basketball, volleyball, soccer, tennis, baseball, rugby, and Ultimate, together with the icebreaker and PE literature. It is a survey of **what is documented**, not an observational study of what coaches actually do, which is a limitation §12 states rather than minimizes.

### 8.2 Scoring convention

One methodological decision has to be declared because it changes the answer. A drill with **no score at all** cannot satisfy property (i): there is a difference between a scoring unit seated on the transfer and no scoring unit at all. The census therefore scores three values rather than two:

- **✓** — the property is actively instantiated by a rule
- **○** — vacuous: the property is not violated, but only because the relevant machinery is absent
- **✗** — violated

Second: property (ii) at **n = 2** is trivially satisfied, because a two-person drill reaches everyone by arithmetic rather than by design. Two-person formats are marked and are not counted as evidence for reach.

### 8.3 The census

### 8.4 The result, stated against the prediction

**Property (i) — transfer as the point: CONFIRMED, with a qualification.** Among formats that score at all, seating the score on the transfer is common and unremarkable: the rondo counts consecutive passes, cooperative tennis counts the rally, pepper counts control, the youth basketball game counts completed passes. The qualification is that **most warm-ups do not score at all**, so the property is more often *vacuous* than *instantiated*. The prediction said "common" and meant instantiated; the honest reading is "common where scoring exists, and scoring often does not."

**Property (iii) — no accumulation: CONFIRMED, and largely for an uninteresting reason.** Warm-ups mostly keep no records because they are warm-ups, not because anyone decided that records were the problem. Where individual counting does appear — shooting lines, batting practice, Queen of the Court — it appears immediately and without apology.

**Property (ii) — reach: FALSIFIED.** The prediction was that reach guarantees would be rare. **They are not rare.** The census found them in at least four distinct architectures:

```
  A. THE QUEUE            three-man weave, rugby line, shooting lines,
                          batting practice
                          → reach by waiting your turn in a line

  B. FIXED ROLE ROTATION  butterfly drill, Ultimate 3-person marking
                          → reach by cycling through positions

  C. ROUND COMPLETION     Name Toss
                          → reach by "everyone receives exactly once"

  D. TURN-TAKING NORM     kemari, chinlone, sepak raga bulatan
                          → reach by an inherited convention of the circle
```

The stated null therefore fires: **the uniqueness claim weakens materially, and this paper reports that before it reports anything else.** The sibling paper's caller mechanism is not the first mechanism to guarantee that everybody touches the ball. It is not close to the first. Coaches have been guaranteeing reach with lines and rotations for as long as there have been lines and rotations.

### 8.5 What survives, explicitly labeled as post-data

The following was arrived at **after** seeing the census and is therefore not a pre-registration, not a confirmed hypothesis, and not entitled to any of the credit the falsified prediction forfeited. It is stated because it is what the data actually shows, and hiding it would be worse than labeling it.

> **The predictability price.** Every reach guarantee found in the census purchases reach with **predictability**. A queue tells you exactly when your turn is coming. A role rotation tells you where you are going next. A memorized name pattern is unpredictable exactly once and then becomes a fixed order by design. The turn-taking norm of the old circle games is a social convention that is legible precisely because it is regular.
>
> **Reach whose order remains unpredictable across unbounded repeated play is unattested in this census.**

**This is not, however, a new idea in this corpus, and the census does not get to claim it as a discovery.** *The Sport That Says Your Name* (2026-07-23) already argued the same point from the armchair, in the course of justifying its own selection policy: *"Equality without randomness would be a queue — predictable, boring, and stigmatizing, since everyone can see whose turn is being given; randomness without equality is every pickup game ever played. The conjunction is the mechanism."* That sentence was written from design reasoning, before any survey existed. **What §8 adds is not the insight but its empirical status**: a claim that had been asserted about the space of possible designs is now a documented finding about the designs that actually exist. The upgrade is from *plausible* to *attested*, which is worth something, and it is considerably less than what a genuinely novel finding would be worth.

Two observations follow, and neither is tested.

**The gap is narrow and specific.** What is unattested is not reach, and not unpredictability, and not name-calling — the Passing Name Game already puts names in a circle, and the Name Toss already closes a round on full coverage. What is unattested is the **conjunction**: reach that is guaranteed, in an order nobody can anticipate, sustained indefinitely rather than for one round, inside an activity that also keeps a score and owns its own ending. Every component exists; the combination does not appear in the surveyed material.

**There may be a reason the combination is missing, and it is not flattering to assume it is oversight.** Guaranteeing reach without a predictable order requires something to *hold* the order — an impartial party who knows whose turn is next and announces it. Before cheap devices, the only available holder was a coach, and a coach calling every single receiver for twenty minutes is a coach doing nothing else. That is a hypothesis about **why** the gap exists, it is untested, and it is exactly the kind of just-so story that a category-defining paper should flag rather than deploy.

There is also a possible mechanism connecting this to §9's falsification, offered as a conjecture with n = 0: **predictable reach and sustained attention may be in tension.** If you know your turn is four away, there is nothing to attend to until then, and the line looks at the ball rather than at each other. If that is right, it would explain why formats in architectures A and B have remained warm-ups for a century — not because they are badly designed, but because a queue is a very good way to distribute touches and a very poor way to hold a room. **We do not know this. It is the most interesting thing the census produced and the least supported.**

## 9 · Drill or Sport?

The category's own life-or-death test, and the definition it requires.

### 9.1 The falsification

> **If the converted forms are only ever played instrumentally — as warm-ups, PE units, means to the competitive game — and never voluntarily for their own sake, then this is not a category of SPORTS. It is a category of DRILLS.**

The census makes this sharper rather than safer. Nearly every mainstream member found in §8 sits inside a practice session, before the real game, and stops when a coach says so. If that is the whole story, the honest conclusion is that circulation is something sports do to warm up, not something a sport can be — and that the three properties describe a preparation phase rather than a class.

### 9.2 The differentia

The test requires knowing what separates the two, and the answer that survives scrutiny is structural rather than attitudinal:

> **A sport owns its own ending. A drill is stopped from outside.**

A drill's boundary is exogenous: the whistle, the coach, the clock on the wall, the start of the real practice. A sport's boundary is endogenous: the ball drops, the count reaches zero, the rules themselves say *that was the end.*

Register it correctly: **this is a differentia within a genus, not a definition of sport.** Within the genus of physical skilled activity it separates drill from sport. It does not distinguish sport from coin-flipping, and owning your ending is **necessary, not sufficient.** Claiming otherwise would be an overclaim this paper cannot carry.

Two rival criteria were considered and are better understood as **consequences** of this one:

- **Terminal vs. instrumental** (*is it played for its own sake?*) is an attitude, so the same activity is a drill for one person and a sport for another. True, unobservable, and unable to define anything.
- **Story vs. capability** (*what does it leave behind?*) is an output, and is the sharpest of the three: a sport is play that generates a story; a drill is play that generates a capability.

The chain that makes the structural criterion primary:

```
   OWNS ITS ENDING  →  HAS A STORY  →  IS WORTH RETURNING TO  →  IS TERMINAL
     (structure)        (output)          (memory)              (attitude)
```

A story requires an ending the activity itself supplied. *"And then the streak died at eighty-seven"* is a story. A drill that stops when the whistle blows has no ending, only an **interruption**, and there is nothing to tell. One structural fact produces the other two.

### 9.3 The staircase

Applied to the institution's own sport, the differentia produces an uncomfortable and clarifying result. Its three modes were designed in July for other reasons entirely, and they line up as a ladder across the drill/sport boundary:

| Mode | Ending condition | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Friendship** | none — it stops when people stop | **a drill** |
| **Streak** | ends when the object drops | **a sport** |
| **Team** | ends at zero | **a sport** |

The floor of the ladder is a drill and this is the correct result, not an embarrassment: the no-score mode is the icebreaker, the first fifteen minutes, the thing you do so that everyone knows each other's names. **The graduation from the no-score mode to the counted one is the exact moment the activity acquires its own ending** — which is to say, becomes a sport.

Note also what this makes of the machinery around a collective streak: park records, the repeated-digit milestones, *"our circle's record is eighty-seven."* Read through the chain above, those are **story-manufacturing equipment bolted onto a warm-up.** An activity engineered to push itself across the drill/sport boundary is a reasonable description of what is being attempted.

### 9.4 The honest counterexample

*"Run the passing drill until someone drops it"* owns its ending and is still called a drill.

This is not a counterexample; it is the thesis in miniature and a confirming instance. The moment you run a drill to a natural ending **and start remembering the number**, you have converted it into a sport. That is precisely the founder's first prediction, restated as a boundary case — and it is the reason the definition makes the drill/sport line **thin and crossable**. Some would call thinness a weakness in a definition. Here it is the claim: a definition that made the line thick would contradict a category that exists at the crossing.

---

## 10 · The Base Rate: Circulation Is Not Cooperation

Every prediction in §11 is, in effect, a prediction that *this time it works.* A pre-registration that omits the base rate is naive, so the base rate goes first.

**Cooperative sport has already been tried as an organized movement, had a real decade, and did not displace competitive sport.**

Terry Orlick's *The Cooperative Sports & Games Book: Challenge Without Competition* (Pantheon, 1978) collected more than a hundred games built on cooperation rather than competition, for every age and setting; it was successful enough to be revised, republished, and followed by a second volume. The **New Games Movement**, emerging from the San Francisco Bay Area in the late 1960s around Stewart Brand, George Leonard, Pat Farrington, Bernie DeKoven and others, ran large public tournaments from 1973 to 1976 that drew thousands, founded the New Games Foundation in 1974, and left a lasting mark on physical education under the motto *Play Hard, Play Fair, Nobody Hurt.* It faded through the 1980s.

Both are prior art of the most direct kind — Orlick's book is, literally, a book of competitive games converted to cooperative ones — and both are the reason this paper cannot honestly describe its category as new. They are also the outcome any new attempt should expect by default.

**The distinction on which everything else here rests:**

> **A cooperative game removes the opponent. A circulation sport keeps the opponent and changes what counts as a point.**

This is not a rhetorical repair. A circulation sport in its adversarial mode still has sides, real opposition, a contested outcome, and a decided ending; what it changes is that the score increments on a *completed transfer* and cannot be incremented by the other side's failure. The opponent is relocated rather than removed — from a person, to the drop, to the circle's own earlier record.

```
   COOPERATIVE GAMES              CIRCULATION SPORTS
   -----------------              ------------------
   opponent REMOVED               opponent KEPT
   nobody loses                   an outcome is decided
   the point is inclusion         the point is the completed transfer
   converts by SUBTRACTION        converts by RE-SEATING the scoring unit
```

If that distinction does not hold under examination, then this paper is a 1978 idea with a new name, and the correct response is to read Orlick instead. We think it holds, for a reason that is testable rather than rhetorical: **a sport can spread where a movement did not.** The cooperative-games movement asked participants to adopt a value. A circulation sport asks them to play a game whose rules happen to have that value built in, against opponents they are still trying to beat. Those are different asks with different adoption curves, and §11 pre-registers the tests.

## 11 · Pre-Registrations

Five predictions, with instruments and stated nulls. **The architecture forbids the obvious instrument**: the reference implementation is local-first with no telemetry by design, so every instrument below is observation, coach or teacher log, or third-party study. *The guards that make the product good make the predictions hard to test, and that is a cost being paid deliberately.*

The four originating predictions were stated by the founder on 2026-08-05 and are preserved verbatim in the project record; three of the four were unfalsifiable as stated (two vacuous conditionals, one secular-trend confound), and the re-specifications below were ratified the same day, **before any data existed**. That ordering is what makes the sharpening legitimate rather than a retrofit.

**P-CS1 — Warm-up extension.** In teams adopting a circulation warm-up (n ≥ 3), median warm-up minutes per session in the final third of a season exceed the first third; and, the stronger instrument, at least one occasion on which **players ask to continue past the coach's stop**. Two further legs test the category rather than the product: **(c)** players run a circle with **no coach present**; **(d)** *who owns the clock* — does the circle play to an ending the game supplies, or to an ending someone supplies? **Null:** flat or declining minutes, no unprompted re-ask, no coach-absent play. Leg (d) requires a single session and is the cheapest instrument in this set.

**P-CS2 — Scoring displacement.** **(a)** In circles that have played ≥ 3 sessions, unscored or count-up sessions outnumber count-down sessions. **Null:** the adversarial mode dominates once unlocked — which is a live possibility, because competition is fun. **(b)** By **2036**, at least one mainstream sport has an officially sanctioned circulatory format played at organized level. **Null:** none has.

**P-CS3 — Participation, as a property of the format.** Offered both a circulatory and a competitive format of the same activity, in the same population at the same time, the circulatory format's sessions are **more gender-mixed and sustain mixed-gender play longer**. **Null:** no difference. The prediction is deliberately about what a format does and never about what any group prefers. Its plausibility rests on the gap in competitive entry being culturally contingent rather than dispositional: Gneezy, Leonard and List (*Econometrica* 77(5), 2009, 1637–1664) found that among the matrilineal Khasi the gender gap in choosing competition **reverses** relative to the patriarchal Maasai. The literature it argues against — Niederle and Vesterlund (*QJE*, 2007) — is itself contested, with meta-analytic work placing the aggregate gap at roughly a third of the original estimate. **If the gap is cultural, a format change is exactly the class of intervention that could move it.**

**P-CS4 — Three generations, under scoring.** Mixed-generation circles **persist when scoring is introduced** — a circle of children, adults, and elders stays mixed after graduating from the unscored mode, rather than re-sorting by age. **Null:** circles age-sort the moment the score appears. This is specified against a counterexample that already exists: **pickleball achieves three-generation play without circulation**, through a low skill floor, a slow ball, and a small court. What pickleball cannot deliver is persistence *under scoring with equal touch*, because targeting the weaker opponent is a legal and standard tactic there — which makes persistence-under-scoring a genuine discriminator rather than a restatement.

**P-CS5 — The warm-up census. ✅ RUN 2026-08-07. RESULT: PARTIAL NULL.** Properties (i) and (iii) confirmed as predicted; **property (ii), reach, predicted rare and found common in four architectures.** The uniqueness claim is narrowed accordingly, and the narrowing is labeled post-data in §8.5. This prediction is closed. Its successor is stated below and is **not** yet run.

**P-CS6 — The predictability price (new, pre-registered here, pre-data).** Across a wider census including observational field data rather than published coaching materials alone, **no reach-guaranteeing format will be found whose receiver order is unpredictable across unbounded repeated play** — excluding formats using an external announcing party, which is the case under test. **Null:** such a format exists and is documented, in which case the residual contribution of the caller mechanism is smaller still and should be restated again.

**The stopping rule.** The full set is reviewed **every 7 January** — a date this institution already keeps for other reasons — and each prediction marked *unrun · running · resolved.* A prediction with no review date is not registered; it is merely written.

## 12 · Honest Limits

**n = 0 for the product; n = 1 for the category's newest member.** No circulation sport designed with this specification in hand has been played by anyone outside a single family. Every claim about adoption, enjoyment, or persistence is untested.

**The census is a desk survey, not fieldwork.** §8 surveyed *published* coaching materials. What coaches actually run, and how much they modify it, is exactly the sort of thing the published record misrepresents. The census's own successor prediction (P-CS6) is stated in the knowledge that field data could overturn §8.5 as readily as §8 overturned P-CS5.

**One prediction in this paper has already failed.** That is stated in §8 rather than buried here, but it belongs in the limits too, because it is evidence about the authors' calibration on precisely the question this paper exists to answer.

**The conjecture in §8.5 about attention and predictability is unsupported.** It is the most interesting output of the census and the least tested claim in the paper.

**The category may be a preparation phase rather than a class.** §9's falsification is real and is not rhetorical hedging. The census found nearly every mainstream member sitting inside a practice session and stopping when a coach says so.

**The distinction from cooperative games carries the entire paper.** If keeping the opponent while re-seating the scoring unit turns out to be a distinction without a difference in practice — if circulation sports are adopted, and abandoned, on the same curve the New Games Movement traced — then the correct conclusion is that Orlick was right, was early, and was thorough, and that this paper added a vocabulary to a settled question.

**The three properties land exactly on three commitments this institution already held.** Give-forward, a dignity floor, and non-accumulation were doctrine before this category was named, and a taxonomy that confirms its author's prior commitments this neatly is either a real discovery or a well-executed projection. From inside, the two are indistinguishable. **The elegance earns the experiment; it does not replace it.**

**Two of the strongest members are living cultural practices with religious and courtly histories.** Kemari and chinlone are described here in the flattened vocabulary of a taxonomy, which is not how their practitioners describe them, and the flattening is a real cost of the method rather than a stylistic choice.

## 13 · Claims and Dedication

Enumerated so that they can be cited, contradicted, or used. All are dedicated to the public domain; **none is a patent claim, and there is nothing here to patent.**

1. **The category.** A class of sports defined by the conjunction of three properties: scoring the completed transfer rather than the termination; guaranteeing reach to every participant as a rule rather than a norm; and accumulating no individual record.
2. **The name.** *Circulation sport*, coined and simultaneously freed, never to be registered as a mark by this institution.
3. **The conversion operator.** The three-step procedure of §5 — re-seat the scoring unit; guarantee reach; delete accumulation — with four worked conversions demonstrating it produces playable games.
4. **The reverse-conversion finding.** That the operator has a documented historical instance running in the opposite direction (sepak raga bulatan → net play, February 1945; standardized as sepak takraw, Kuala Lumpur, 1960), which establishes the operation as real and its direction as a choice.
5. **The boundary.** The negative space of §6, in particular that Ultimate Frisbee is excluded because Spirit of the Game governs conduct rather than the scoring unit, and that the rondo fails on reach because it has a designated loser.
6. **The warm-up identity.** That the operator's outputs already exist, unrecognized as a family, as the warm-ups and youth rules of the sports they were derived from — which makes the category empirical rather than speculative.
7. **The census method and its result**, including the falsification of the authors' own prediction that reach guarantees are rare, and the four reach architectures it documents.
8. **The predictability price** (post-data, §8.5): that every attested reach guarantee purchases reach with predictability, and that reach with an unpredictable order sustained across unbounded play is unattested. **Claimed as an empirical finding only** — the underlying design argument (*equality without randomness is a queue; the conjunction is the mechanism*) belongs to *The Sport That Says Your Name* (2026-07-23) and is cited, not re-claimed.
9. **The drill/sport differentia.** *A sport owns its own ending; a drill is stopped from outside* — offered as necessary and not sufficient within the genus of physical skilled activity, together with the derivation chain of §9.2 and the mode-ladder application of §9.3.
10. **The circulation ≠ cooperation distinction**, as the specific reason this category is not the cooperative-games movement under a new name, and as the claim on which the paper's predictions stand or fall.

---

## 14 · Closing

The oldest game in this paper is fourteen centuries old and was preserved because an emperor paid for it to survive. The newest is a folk game played at dusk in Cambodian streets, which nobody has ever thought to preserve because it never occurred to anyone that it might not.

Between those two there is a family of games that were never collected, on four continents, in languages that did not borrow from one another, all of which independently arrived at the same idea: **that the interesting thing about an object passing between people is the passing, and that the moment it stops is not a victory but simply the end.**

We have named that family and written down how to make more of them. Whether anyone should is a question the next decade answers, and the answer is not in our hands — which is the correct place for it, and the reason the procedure is given away rather than kept.

---

*Authored by Thon Ly with Miss Aquarius℠. Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0. Comments, corrections, and above all counterexamples are welcome; a category is only as good as the members it correctly refuses.*

Two consequences follow free — *apacāyana* atop *veyyāvacca* when the beneficiary is a parent or elder, and **the dead reached by the identical structure**, which makes ancestral observance a native instance rather than an adjacent practice. ⚠️ **The limit is stated with it and is not closed: the path needs two attendees, and both cases this paper cites for *complete anyway* are solitary.** One guard is added — such a beneficiary may never become a destination in §5.2's menu. **No numbered claim changes and no prior-art clock starts.**
